transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 17:00:00Z
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maria Alvarez (Pegasus Head of SRE), Diego Ramos (Pegasus Infra Lead), Lena Chen (Pegasus Security), Tom Baker (Pegasus VP Product)

Summary (auto): quick follow-up after the 2026-11-28 outage impacting tokenization and KV cache warm-up. Discussed mitigations (autoscale policy tuning, prefix caching, fallback model variant), next steps for load-testing on Redwood Dedicated, and security artifacts requested by Pegasus.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're keeping this tight — about 45 minutes — to go over the postmortem follow-up from last week. Maria, do you want to kick off with any top concerns?

[00:18] Maria Alvarez: Yeah thanks Alex. Main thing: customers saw increased latency and a few 5xxs on the payments path around 11/28. We got the immediate mitigation, but team wants to understand root cause, what permanent fixes are coming, and when we can expect stability for production traffic. Also, security wants the KMS/SSO answers.

[00:40] Alex Kim: Totally. Priya and I ran the initial RCA with traces. Short summary: traffic spike hit a cold KV cache + slightly aggressive scale-down setting; that combined with a model tokenization path change caused longer per-token compute and queued requests. There was also a fallback routing misconfiguration for the smaller model variant so a subset of requests retried to the same overloaded host. Not one single thing, multiple fail modes.

[01:12] Priya Desai: Yeah to add — our telemetry shows a spike in KV cache misses for prefixes we hadn't warmed after the deploy. The serving runtime then tried to rehydrate the KV which blocks some token generation loops, adds latency. Couple that with the autoscaler cooldown set to 30s and we hit CPU/GPU pressure. Some requests then timed out at the LB and retried.

[01:45] Diego Ramos: Quick question — when you say tokenization path change, was that a model update from your side or something in the runtime?

[01:55] Priya Desai: It was a model artifact — the new tokenizer for the updated model variant introduced slightly different chunking, which increased average sequence length by a small percent for payment prompts. We should've flagged that in the deploy but it slipped past QA.

[02:14] Maria Alvarez: Right, that explains the latency delta. For our side, the big ask is a deterministic plan: how do we avoid this cascade — tokenization -> cache miss -> autoscale lag -> timeouts.

[02:28] Alex Kim: Understood. High level mitigation plan we discussed: 1) adjust autoscale policy for your dedicated pool (longer scale-up aggressiveness, shorter cooldown on scale-up), 2) proactive KV prefix warm-up for known critical prefixes during deploys, 3) introduce a short-term routing fallback to a smaller, lower-latency model variant when latency thresholds cross, and 4) replay and load-test your traffic on Dedicated to validate.

[03:05] Tom Baker: On point 3, wanted to call out product risk — fallback to smaller model must preserve quality for payments flows. We don't want false positives/faulty classification.

[03:20] Priya Desai: Agreed — fallback will be guarded by a quality gate. We'll run swift A/B tests using the eval harness you shared earlier and only enable automatic fallback when pass rates are within agreed thresholds. We'll also preserve a ring for manual failover during initial days.

[03:40] Lena Chen: Security here — we also need to confirm whether any persisted logs during the incident included PII and how long traces are retained. Also want to see KMS integration docs — are keys customer-managed?

[03:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, that's on our list. We'll share a short security Q&A doc that covers SOC2 scope, retention, and KMS options. For Pegasus Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via the KMS integration; Jordan will drop the details.

[04:12] Maria Alvarez: Thanks. Can you also share the Prometheus queries or traces so we can map to our internal alerts?

[04:22] Alex Kim: Absolutely. Action item: I'll send over the latency + error-rate graphs and the trace IDs from the incident window by Friday.

[05:00] (brief cross talk)

[05:30] Priya Desai: For the longer-term reliability work we've already queued: - autoscaler policy changes as config flags, - cache warm-up hooks in our deploy pipeline, - stronger pre-deploy profiling for tokenizer/model changes, and - better fallbacks in the routing layer so retries don't hit the same overloaded hosts. We'll put timelines in the doc.

[06:05] Diego Ramos: For the cache warm-up — how invasive is that? We don't want warm-up to add a big window to deploys.

[06:15] Priya Desai: The warm-up would be optional per-deploy and targeted — you provide a small set of critical prefixes (payments prompts); we warm those in parallel and only block rollout for the canary if warm-up fails after a short timeout. It should be a few seconds per prefix, not minutes.

[06:40] Maria Alvarez: Sounds reasonable. Also want to set an SLO: <200ms p95 for token generation on payments path. We can iterate, but that is our baseline ask.

[06:55] Alex Kim: Noted. We'll use that SLO for the Dedicated tests.

[07:10] Tom Baker: One other thing: cost impact of these changes? Longer scale-up and pre-warm implies higher short-term cost. We're okay but want clear numbers.

[07:22] Priya Desai: We'll provide an estimate — tradeoffs: pre-warm + slightly larger headroom increases cost ~5-12% depending on burst profile, but reduces risk of customer-impacting errors which from your data looks more costly. We'll run the Dedicated test with cost telemetry so you can see the delta.

[07:44] Alex Kim: Concrete next steps recap — (1) Alex to share graphs and trace IDs, (2) Priya to run two scaling experiments on a Redwood Dedicated pool using your production-like traffic profile and share results, (3) Jordan to drop the security/KMS doc, (4) Maria to confirm SLOs and any additional prefixes for warm-up.

[08:08] Maria Alvarez: We'll also coordinate a window for the load test — likely a low-traffic slot next week.

[08:18] Diego Ramos: On the load test, can Redwood simulate the client-side retry pattern? Our clients use a 500ms retry with jitter. If that isn't simulated we'll miss the cascading behavior.

[08:30] Priya Desai: Good call — we'll parameterize the test to match your retry backoff and jitter and replicate the sequence length distribution we saw. Please send the exact client retry settings and we'll mirror them.

[08:50] Lena Chen: Quick compliance ask — we need a written statement that logs containing PII were not retained beyond X days and the steps to verify.

[09:03] Jordan Lee: We'll include that in the security doc. For PII retention we can provide retention policy and evidence snippets for the relevant retention window.

[09:18] (pause)

[09:30] Alex Kim: Diving into proposed mitigations, starting with autoscale: Priya, can you walk through the specific policy changes?

[09:40] Priya Desai: Sure — change 1: reduce scale-down aggressiveness (longer cool-down) to avoid oscillation post-burst. Change 2: increase initial replica headroom for deploys of new model variants to account for tokenization delta. Change 3: enable burst capacity throttle that allows a short-overflow by spinning up extra instances faster for a defined window. We'll provide a config diff.

[10:15] Maria Alvarez: How will we test policy 3 without impacting production?

[10:22] Priya Desai: We'll run it first on a Dedicated replica set and do the replay/chaos tests. If it passes, we can roll to production with a canary.

[10:36] Diego Ramos: About the fallback routing — earlier you mentioned retries all going to same host, why was that happening?

[10:44] Priya Desai: The routing stickiness key was based on model shard id which didn't change after retries; we need a better retry-aware hashing or a dedicated retry bucket. Fix is a small router change.

[11:00] Tom Baker: Timeline for router change?

[11:05] Priya Desai: Small change — we can patch in 1 week, QA/Triage + canary in 2 weeks. We'll prioritize if you want it earlier.

[11:18] Maria Alvarez: Prioritize it. That one seems high-leverage.

[11:25] Alex Kim: Great. Anything else on mitigations?

[11:30] Lena Chen: On KMS: confirm if Pegasus Dedicated can use a customer-managed key (CMK) and the rotation schedule. Also want details on audit logs for key usage.

[11:40] Jordan Lee: Yes, Dedicated supports CMKs; rotation schedule is customer-controlled via your KMS. We'll include steps for verifying key usage via audit logs.

[11:55] Maria Alvarez: Perfect. Last block — communication and SLAs. If we do the above, what's the expected time to return to normal error budget?

[12:06] Alex Kim: After the dedicated tests and router fix, our estimate is within 2-3 weeks we can get p95 latency back under 200ms with the warm-up and autoscale changes. We'll be conservative until tests are done.

[12:25] Tom Baker: OK. We want a formal follow-up meeting after the load test to sign off.

[12:31] Alex Kim: Jordan, can you set that up?

[12:34] Jordan Lee: Yep — will schedule a 60-minute sign-off slot for the week after the tests.

[12:42] (wrap-up)

[12:50] Alex Kim: Recap of action items and owners — I've got them captured; you'll get the notes and links in the shared folder. Anything else from Pegasus?

[13:00] Maria Alvarez: No, that's it. Appreciate the quick response and the clearer plan.

[13:08] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll be in touch — look out for the security doc and latency graphs.

(End meeting)
